items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: It’s an interesting book, Stravinsky, Poetics of Music.

ctx.x: Does that have anything to do with the way you write?

Probably. It’s an interesting book, Stravinsky, Poetics of Music. And that’s I think one of the most important sentences that a musician, a young musician, should really look at and try and digest because selective improvisation — composition is selective improvisation. And that connects the composer and the jazz musician in a wonderful way in that it’s the same kind of mindset that plays jazz as composes and writes music. But you haven’t got time to be selective. You have to move to the next note in a split…
Yeah. You can go back and edit things that you might have done on the spot and you liked part of it perhaps.
